# cao01: task-scoped ally occupancy, with failed-route relaxation

**Review draft: do not queue until campaign-owner review.**

Parent commit `87144776ee5402991fbc05d2ccd67ffc74e05bd6`, base bot
`pi_dominant-live-progress-01`. Candidate directory
`bots/pi_camp-ally-occupancy-01/` only. Copy that exact parent, not original g07,
dp01 or another experimental branch. Add `IMPLEMENTATION.md` with source scope,
tests actually run, query/field bounds and limitations. Do not run games or upload.

## Problem, evidence and hypothesis

The parent won all4 local Vault games but failed its developmental gates:
champion A capture349/bank367, B264/284, versus required A<200/<250 and
B<=215/<=238. A central damage through100 is1310, but Marcella contributes only65:
15HP at17 and50HP at26, then no central damage through100. She alternates move
endpoints(9,18)/(10,19) every round27–91. B Marcella alternates(20,12)/(20,11)
25–51, then resumes some work; central damage through100 is300.

The actual local cause has two components. A(9,18) sees12 living central members;
A(10,19) sees no central spawn tiles. The latter skips `World::refresh` and
`camp_goals` takes its stale-seen all-spawn approach. More decisively, Heart at
A(11,16) changes from local known15 to known8/position(-1,-1), although actual
Heart stays there22/input342 through91/input1283. On B the same happens to Heart
at(19,14), globally stationary20/input316 through53/input788. SDK
`vision::champion_tiles` means visible occupancy; rebuilding `Snapshot::blocked`
drops that hidden ally and opens an apparent shortcut back through the choke.

Exact-source goal fixtures show that remembering living goals alone still
reverses both steps. Retaining only the last locally observed Heart tile moves
A(10,19)->(11,20), B(20,11)->(19,10). Official engine shadowcasting plus own wards
reconstructs all15 local probe masks exactly. Subsequent static-world tests show
TTL1 merely creates four-step loops; TTL2–5 remains unreliable. Retaining
observations until contradicted reaches a visible central attack opportunity in
14walks on both sides, but a stale hidden cut vertex can make a route permanently
unreachable. Deferred uncertain-only relaxation fixes that synthetic impasse
after one failed attempt. This is research evidence, not a simulated bot win.

**Hypothesis:** a small private ally-observation module, scoped to one committed
living-camp task, preserves correct blocker information across personal-vision
loss; on proven route failure it forgets uncertain evidence before the next
normal round's attempt. This advances actual camp work without inventing hidden
positions or indefinitely blocking an open passage.

An earlier dlp health-progress claim was withdrawn: the hidden-side frames have
zero visible group spawn tiles, so refresh skips rather than raising remainingHP.
Do not change health/progress calculation on the basis of that invalid claim.

## Production contract

Implement one module with a small interface for (a) preparing a task-scoped
uncertain blocker overlay from a complete current owned observation batch and
(b) accepting an attempt result with the exact record token used. Keep entry
versioning/reset/deferred deletion inside the module. Native tests should cross
this same interface; no copied cache-policy calculation in place of production.

Entries: one last positive position per allied roster identity excluding self,
plus observation round/revision and validity. Bound storage by actual roster
size. No enemy history, global replay input, shared-memory position protocol,
camp-member ledger or map-sized persistent history. Key scope by own life,
committed camp identity and `task_started`. Clear on key change, no task, own
death, or camp reward/respawn. Existing90-round task limit bounds applicability;
do not add an age TTL or alter task/stall timers.

Capture visible ally **value positions once** from the existing visible ally
enumeration. Prefer its owning tile positions instead of fetching
`champion.position()` repeatedly for caching. Publish the batch only if its
round/observation revision remains current after collection. Stage updates until
that check succeeds. Use bounded before/after batch guards, not one extra
round/fuel guard for every SDK getter; preserve current no-stale-action guards.
Do not turn this into a whole-observation rewrite or a new query-heavy dispatcher.

Current positive positions replace old positions. Seeing the old tile clear
removes that record; seeing another live unit there must still retain the current
unit in the fresh blocker mask. Known death removes the entry; never retain self
as an obstacle. Independent `champion.is_alive()` is allowed for a retained hidden
ally, never hidden `position()`/live-info queries. Bound new alive checks to at
most once per retained hidden entry per round; current visible positives satisfy
that round's alive evidence. Record actual call-count tests. Rollover/query
failure must not fabricate a current observation or death; preserve unrelated
error handling. Do not refresh timestamps by reading/applying cached data.

Only ordinary navigation toward the currently committed **living** camp receives
the overlay. Keep it separate from canonical `Snapshot::blocked`; banking,
escape, combat, selectors and exploration must not silently inherit it. Camp
reward navigation retains its existing behavior. Original current blockers are
always unioned independently and can never be removed by cache relaxation.

### Attempt outcomes and deferred deletion

- After a **complete current** `no_route_now` with uncertain entries used,
  schedule only those matching uncertain record versions for deletion no earlier
  than the next round's normal navigation attempt. No extra same-round field.
- If fresh nonempty goals are eliminated solely by the uncertain overlay, treat
  that as the same relaxable failure. Distinguish it from goals already empty or
  invalid without the overlay; the latter supplies no occupancy inference.
- `deferred`, stale epoch, incomplete field, `wait`, `at_goal` and successful
  movement do not schedule failure deletion. Do not interpret budget exhaustion
  as proof of no route.
- Pending deletion is conditional on entry revision/position/observation token.
  A fresher observation wins, including one later in the same round. Never
  reconstruct deleted entries from old snapshots. Only a new positive observation
  may add them again.
- Clearing/retaining evidence, route failure and waiting never directly update
  `memory.progressed`, `last_distance` or task timestamps. Keep actual action and
  health-progress rules unchanged. Existing stall8/task90 remain unchanged.

Normal field admission/limits and checked movement stay in force. Do not change
shortest-path ordering, add a route/waypoint planner, forbid reversing direction,
change camp scores/goals, combat/roster/ward behavior, or add logging in production.
Preserve `Config::coordination=false` and the inherited8byte wire layout for this
experiment. That preservation is experiment scope, not a user prohibition on
future separately researched communication.

Expected source surface: a private occupancy module plus minimal observation
value capture and camp-navigation integration. Changes to `objectives.cpp`,
combat, economy, draft, protocol and tuning constants are not expected; justify
any necessary interface-only edit, and do not silently broaden behavior.

## Native contract checks required on Pi

Compile/test the actual candidate module and the actual production camp navigation
integration; source-body extraction with explicit host adapters is acceptable.
Do not test only a copied estimator or only the original parent.

1. Positive visible ally -> hidden tile retains the record for this task without
   querying hidden position. Reuse never renews its timestamp. Unknown entries,
   self/enemy IDs, invalid/future/incomplete observations cannot add blockers.
2. Visible moved/clear/dead evidence invalidates exactly the old identity. Another
   currently visible unit on that tile remains blocked. Own life/task identity,
   `task_started`, reward/respawn and absent-task transitions clear applicability.
3. Failed route schedules deletion only for uncertain versions used, never current
   visible blockers. Same-round calls still retain them. Next-round deletion does
   not erase an intervening fresh revision. Already-empty goals and overlay-caused
   empty goals are distinguished. Deferred/stale/incomplete results do not clear.
4. Batch rollover before/after collection publishes no partial new positions and
   performs no stale move. Bound alive queries per entry per round and field
   count; no extra same-turn field solely to try the relaxed mask.
5. Call actual `camp_action` and actual `task_expired`: no-route/deferred/
   invalid-goals/forget-only do not credit progress; actual moved-distance credit,
   stall8 and task90 remain unchanged. Preserve ordinary non-camp behavior.
6. A blocked corridor must permit necessary backtracking after replanning. Do not
   repair oscillation by banning the previous tile or ignoring current blockers.

The parent source invariant fixture exists locally on the campaign PC at
`tools/diagnostics/run_occupancy_progress_fixture.py`; its host refresh is
unchanged-health and navigation results scripted. The candidate must test its
own implementation, not cite that parent receipt as its own pass.

## Frozen geometry acceptance, before PC games

The campaign PC will feed actual production occupancy decisions through the
existing official-visibility continuation driver. Pi should provide a small
native test adapter to the module's same interface (owned current values,
task/life key, attempt feedback -> resulting uncertain tile mask); document how
to compile/invoke it. The agent must not need `.cambc` PC replay assets to implement
the above contract. Geometry/replay controls are the PC reviewer's responsibility;
do not replace them with invented source coordinates or claim to have run them.

All conditions below are fixed, movement-only frozen-world controls. "Service"
means a currently visible living central camp within basic attack range, not a
capture/win. Upper bounds are successful walking steps, with no repeated state
or attempted move into a frozen occupied destination:

| Condition | A maximum | B maximum |
|---|---:|---:|
| Actual stationary Heart local boundary |14 |14 |
| Additional unit on first detour step |15 |15 |
| Positively known dead Heart |4 |3 |
| Hidden Heart move controls |14 (at most+10 vs visible-only) |14 (at most+11) |

A hidden-move destinations are(12,15),(12,16),(12,17); B are(18,14),(18,15).
Visible-moved controls must retain the original short walk: A(10,15)/(10,16)
<=4,(10,17)<=5; B(20,13)<=4,(20,14)/(20,15)<=3. These acknowledge real stale-detour
cost; they are not a global guarantee. A phantom hidden cut vertex must cost at
most one failed normal attempt before the uncertain mask is relaxed on the next
round, then use the open path. Current/live cut vertices must remain blocked.
No extra field in the failed round. Static no-route without uncertainty must
remain failure and may use the original expiry behavior.

## Frozen PC release protocol

Only after source/native/geometry review: exact CLI5/engine3 release, normal fuel,
**four Vault games**, champion and C02 on both sides, same map/seed/build as parent.
Do not run standard80 first. Preserve exact source/WASM/ZIP identity and receipts.

- Zero candidate VM faults; zero newly caught SDK errors. Investigate any failure,
  including stale/hidden ally lookups, before considering a pass.
- At least3/4 wins.
- Champion A central first capture<200 and first subsequent positive own bank by
  a recipient of that first capture<250.
- Champion B central first capture<=215 and corresponding bank<=238. These are
  retained earlier targets, deliberately stricter than dlp01's264/284.
- Champion A central HP removed through100>1080 (retained gate), plus Marcella's
  own central damage A>65 and B>=300. Teammates doing all the work is insufficient.
- Actual release mechanism: inspect the first action divergence and the actual
  post-partial-kill trajectory. Do not assume the original29/27 boundaries recur.
  Require continued useful central work and no sustained short-position cycle:
  through round100, while alive, empty-bag, no covering awake damaging camp or
  global enemy within Chebyshev6 and central work remains, reject a Marcella
  zero-central-damage movement segment
  containing at least two repetitions of a position period2–12 and at least
  eight successful moves. These conditions are audited from replay; private task
  IDs or source-level fuel locations are not inferred.

Any failed gate stops expansion. Native/model passes alone are insufficient. If
all pass, the campaign owner freezes a separate regression panel before any
additional games. No platform submission, ranked-selection change or promotion
from these four games. Original confirmation maps remain consumed evidence.
implementation_report:
# cao01: task-scoped ally occupancy

Review candidate only. Base commit: `87144776ee5402991fbc05d2ccd67ffc74e05bd6`; parent source: `bots/pi_dominant-live-progress-01/`. Changes remain uncommitted for the bridge. No games, uploads, submission, promotion or release build were performed.

## Hypothesis and source scope

Retaining the last personally observed ally position during one committed living-camp task should prevent a hidden stationary ally from repeatedly reopening an apparent choke shortcut. When a complete current navigation attempt proves no route with uncertain evidence, forgetting those exact uncertain versions on a later round's normal attempt should release a phantom obstruction.

This implements the supplied occupancy hypothesis. It makes no new health/progress claim: zero visible spawn tiles still skip World::refresh, and the parent's health/progress implementation is unchanged.

Production differences, compared byte-for-byte with the exact base parent's source:

- New `src/ally_occupancy.h`: SDK-independent private cache with owned observation batches, scope keys, exact versioned attempt tokens and conditional deferred deletion.
- `src/observations.h/.cpp`: capture ally identities and tile value positions from the same owning tile/champion_at enumeration used by SDK vision::champions. Keep the existing champion list for existing consumers. Complete the batch only across successful round/revision guards; publish staged cache updates only across a second bounded guard pair. Retain current visibility values for clear-tile evidence. The small adapter queries only roster handles' is_alive for hidden retained entries.
- `src/navigation.h/.cpp`: optional uncertain-mask input and overlay-empty result flag. Canonical current blockers are filtered independently before unioning uncertainty. Existing field search, distance ordering, walking/dash selection, checked moves, yield behavior, retry and admission limits remain in place. A stale/incomplete occupancy observation or stale field returns deferred. Defaults preserve ordinary callers.
- `src/bot.cpp`: initialize the private roster adapter, synchronize life/task/task_started scope and clear on abandonment or nonliving/absent task. Feed only living-camp travel an overlay and return exact attempt feedback. Observation publication also runs after movement, so a fresher same-round sighting supersedes pending deletion. Reward navigation uses the existing ordinary call behavior.

No edits to objectives, combat, economy, draft, protocol, tuning constants, other bots, SDK, repository tools or settings. `Config::coordination=false`, inherited eight-byte wire format, stall8/task90 and action/health-based progress rules remain unchanged. `SOURCE_SHA256SUMS` now describes this candidate's source, including the new header.

Reviewed strategy overview, state machine, navigation and camp-selection documents, historical meta strategy, SDK compatibility notes, game rules and actual C++ champion/vision/distance-field declarations.

## Policy and bounds

One entry per actual allied roster identity excluding self; unknown and enemy identities cannot insert records. Each entry holds at most one positive tile, original observation round/revision, private version, alive-probe round and one pending exact-version deletion. Scope changes clear applicability internally. There is no age TTL, enemy history, shared position protocol, camp-member ledger or persistent map history. The existing 90-round task limit bounds applicability.

A complete current positive replaces the old identity position; old-tile visibility without that identity removes it. Current occupants remain in Snapshot::blocked independently. A positive observation provides that round's alive evidence. Otherwise a retained hidden entry gets at most one new is_alive query per round, including an unknown/error response. Probe-attempt accounting survives rejected publication; stale death/position evidence does not. Expected api_not_in_vision/api_not_found probes remain unknown; unrelated errors propagate. No hidden position or live-info query is added.

Storage is O(roster), apart from the current observation's owned positives and current visible-tile values. The latter are snapshot data, not accumulated map history. Batch collection uses two round/revision boundaries, not a guard per getter. Cache preparation uses another two boundaries. No field is added by the module. Existing maximum three fields and admission/reserve constants remain unchanged. A failed complete field uses one normal field; overlay-only elimination of nonempty fresh goals needs zero. Relaxation never triggers an immediate retry or a second field.

Feedback schedules only uncertain records matching the attempt's scope, observation and full record token. Current visible records cannot be scheduled. Same-round calls retain scheduled records. Later-round normal preparation applies deletion only after incorporating new positives, so a fresh revision wins. Observation-only publication never applies pending deletion. Reusing a hidden record never renews its observation timestamp. Deferred/stale results, wait, at_goal and movement do not schedule deletion; already-empty goals provide no inference. Failure, retaining and forgetting never directly alter progress/distance/task timestamps.

## Checks actually run on Pi

Host: aarch64, GCC 13.3.0. All commands below passed from repository root:

```sh
python3 bots/pi_camp-ally-occupancy-01/tests/run_occupancy.py
python3 bots/pi_camp-ally-occupancy-01/tests/run_native.py
g++ -std=c++20 -Wno-changes-meaning -include cmath -fsyntax-only -I sdk/cpp bots/pi_camp-ally-occupancy-01/src/*.cpp
```

The new runner compiles the actual module with `-std=c++20 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror`. It extracts unmodified production prepare_camp_occupancy, observe, navigation declarations/TurnBudget, move_to and camp_action bodies; explicit host adapters supply SDK values, a small walking BFS field and action results. Memory, Config and task_expired are actual production code. No copied cache estimator or parent occupancy receipt stands in for the candidate. Generated headers and binaries stay in temporary directories.

Verified module identity filtering, invalid/out-of-bounds/future/incomplete batches, retained hidden timestamps, moved/clear/dead evidence, all key transitions, exact uncertain-only feedback, same-round retention, next-round deletion, fresh same-round revision protection, and stale/incomplete/other feedback rejection. Actual call-count assertions: zero alive probes for positive visible entries; one for the first hidden use, zero additional probes on same-round reuse; one on the following hidden round; one unknown-result probe across same-round revisions; one stale-post-probe attempt without publishing its death or repeating that round's query.

Production integration checks cover rollover before/during/after ally collection, field round/revision rollover, no stale move, expected query failures versus propagated unrelated errors, actual camp_action no-route/deferred/empty-goal/overlay-empty/at_goal/wait paths, and unchanged progress. The phantom corridor consumes one field on its failed invocation, retains uncertainty on another same-round invocation, and walks on the next round after relaxation. Movement reducing distance credits progress; failed/forget-only paths do not. Actual task_expired enforces stall8 and task90. Necessary backtracking is permitted. Ordinary navigation ignores private uncertainty, reward/respawn/absent-task transitions clear applicability, and current blockers remain blocked.

The inherited runner additionally passed 84 dominant metadata/selection checks, protocol/state scenarios, 19 production combat/reference scenarios and committed refresh/progress regressions. Those health regressions are inherited compatibility checks, not occupancy or release evidence. Early new-test runs exposed host-adapter compilation mistakes; those were corrected before the final passing run.

## Native PC geometry adapter

Compile without SDK or replay assets:

```sh
g++ -std=c++20 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Werror \
  -I bots/pi_camp-ally-occupancy-01/src \
  bots/pi_camp-ally-occupancy-01/tests/occupancy_adapter.cpp \
  -o /tmp/cao01-occupancy-adapter
/tmp/cao01-occupancy-adapter < observations.txt
```

Whitespace-delimited commands, one process per champion:

- `roster SELF COUNT ID...`: initialize actual allied roster, including self.
- `key LIFE TASK TASK_STARTED`: synchronize committed living-camp scope; use TASK=-1 for death, absent task, reward or respawn.
- `batch ROUND REVISION COMPLETE WIDTH HEIGHT NORMAL NP [ID X Y]... NV [X Y]... NA [ID ALIVE]...`: complete owned current positives, current visible tiles and independent hidden-alive answers. ALIVE is 1/0/-1 (alive/dead/unknown). NORMAL=0 publishes an observation; NORMAL=1 prepares a normal navigation attempt and permits due deletion. COMPLETE=0 cannot publish. The adapter treats the supplied round/revision as the host's current epoch.
- `feedback OUTCOME ROUND REVISION COMPLETE`: feed back the last emitted attempt token. OUTCOME=0 for every nonfailure, 1 for complete no_route_now, 2 for goals eliminated solely by uncertainty. Stale/incomplete feedback is rejected by the same module.

Every batch emits `mask CURRENT ALIVE_QUERY_COUNT N [ID X Y OBS_ROUND OBS_REV RECORD_VERSION]...`, listing uncertain records whose tiles must be unioned with the independent current blocker mask. The runner compiles this adapter and smoke-tests positive -> hidden -> failed feedback -> next-round empty mask. PC geometry must supply official visibility and its existing movement/goal controls; this adapter contains no invented replay coordinates or visibility reconstruction.

## Remaining review gates

Native tests use explicit host adapters, not the official VM or shadowcasting. Full WASM linking, engine fuel/runtime costs, official-visibility continuation geometry, frozen A/B walk bounds, actual first divergence, replay cycle audit, champion damage/capture/bank timings, VM/SDK-error receipts and the four Vault games were not run. No native result establishes those gates or a simulated bot win. The PC reviewer and campaign owner retain geometry/replay controls and the frozen release protocol. Do not queue or expand this review draft on native passes alone.

test_report.decision: Rejected before release games: failed move reveals relocated ally; recursive navigation reuses contradicted occupancy mask.
